records.reason: m141 at 1/1 and 150 ul starts a fixed-loading solvent-response pair. Predicted endpoints of 9.18/31.09 mL test whether substantial retention persists in 50% EA for the lutidine scaffold highlighted by recent feedback.

Pair m141 at 5/1 with its selected 1/1 experiment, holding every loading variable fixed. Predicted endpoints rise to 17.47/37.96 mL. These labels locate the response below the previously measured 10/1 condition.

m66 in pure EA predicts 6.60/13.98 mL and matches the loading conditions of its measured 1/1 example. This stronger-eluent anchor tests how readily the prolonged completion revealed in recent feedback disappears.

Novel para-aminobenzonitrile m160 at 2/1 supplies a baseline for the matched 5/1 experiment. The available meta-isomer observations offer a structural reference, with sample-amount differences kept explicit.

The matched m160 5/1 point predicts V2 48.44 mL versus 31.20 mL at 2/1. Measuring both identifies a response slope for an uncovered amino-aromatic environment and tests transfer beyond a generic nitrogen offset.
Novel dibenzylamine m212 at 2/1 begins a controlled response pair with 5/1. Its predicted 6.84/14.72 mL endpoints establish the ordinary-retention side of the model's sharp predicted transition.

At unchanged loading, m212 at 5/1 predicts 27.50/36.69 mL. Together with its 2/1 baseline, this tests whether secondary-amine retention has the predicted steep response and whether onset and completion shift together.

Novel fluorinated beta-dicarbonyl m167 at 50/1 predicts early onset with prolonged completion, 9.27/30.75 mL. Its label tests transfer of endpoint behavior across dicarbonyl environments and aromatic substitution.

m125 at 5/1, 100 mg and 300 ul DCM loading volume is one side of a volume-only contrast. It tests whether the loading-volume relationship suggested elsewhere in the trajectory persists at another mobile-phase ratio.

The paired m125 experiment changes only DCM loading volume from 300 to 500 ul. Predictions remain essentially identical at 18.31/38.15 mL. The contrast can reveal a neglected interaction or weaken its proposed reproducibility.

m177 at 5/1 and 50 ul sample volume starts a controlled amount contrast. The earlier weak-eluent loading discrepancy makes this useful for testing whether amount sensitivity diminishes at higher EA fraction.

Pair m177 at 5/1 and 150 ul with the selected 50 ul experiment, holding density, loading solvent and its volume fixed. Both predict V2 near 26.86 mL, directly challenging the model's near invariance to amount.
Novel p-methylbenzyl alcohol m135 at 5/1 begins a fixed-loading response pair. Predicted endpoints of 23.06/39.18 mL test primary-alcohol transfer to a simple benzylic environment.
The matched m135 10/1 point predicts 41.72/76.57 mL. The two labels test its steep predicted response as EA fraction decreases and distinguish errors in onset from errors in completion.

Novel 1-phenylethanol m61 at 5/1 predicts 14.37/20.96 mL. It tests transfer into a secondary benzylic-alcohol environment under PE loading and provides a useful comparison with the primary-alcohol probes.

Novel 1-phenylpropanol m67 at 20/1 predicts 32.86/54.78 mL. It extends secondary-alcohol coverage into weaker eluent. Different loading conditions from m61 mean their comparison informs the joint structure-condition mapping.
Novel alpha-hydroxy ester m99 at 5/1 predicts 10.87/19.38 mL. Its hydroxyl-carbonyl environment and 1000 ul DCM loading volume test transfer between alcohol and ester chemistry.

Cinnamic acid m173 adds an uncovered conjugated carboxylic-acid environment at 5/1 with 2000 ul DCM loading volume. Its label expands this joint chemistry-loading region without claiming to isolate an acid effect.

m206 at 5/1 and 100 ul predicts 39.40/73.47 mL. It extends an available 2/1 measurement at identical loading conditions, directly testing the predicted solvent response of a naphthylmethanol scaffold.

Related naphthyl alcohol m205 at 5/1 and 100 ul predicts 46.47/89.30 mL. Comparison with the available 150 ul measurement tests amount transfer in a late-retention family and complements the m206 condition extension.

m13 at 1/1 and 150 ul supplies the higher-EA baseline for a matched 5/1 experiment. Its ordinary prediction, 3.52/8.19 mL, sharply contrasts with the second selected condition and tests where the predicted transition occurs.

The matched m13 5/1 point predicts 35.34/63.86 mL. This pair tests whether the multifunctional-carbonyl failure revealed earlier corresponds to a sharp, learnable response to mobile-phase composition.
Novel methylenedioxy acetophenone m39 at 10/1 starts a controlled pair with 20/1. Predicted endpoints of 18.75/36.63 mL test transfer into a rigid three-acceptor aromatic-carbonyl environment.

At identical loading, m39 at 20/1 predicts 32.68/58.18 mL. The paired labels establish whether this late response is real and whether onset and completion change proportionally as eluent strength decreases.
Novel p-methoxybenzaldehyde m118 at 10/1 predicts 18.21/41.80 mL. Pairing it with 5/1 tests an uncovered aldehyde response curve and the substantial retention assigned to this scaffold.
The matched m118 5/1 point predicts 9.80/28.53 mL. It supplies a lower-ratio anchor and a methoxy-aldehyde reference for the selected methylthio aldehyde, while keeping loading differences explicit.

Novel p-methylthio acetophenone m128 at 5/1 predicts 11.85/23.13 mL. Alongside the selected methoxy ketone, it tests oxygen-to-sulfur transfer within aromatic ketones, accounting for density-derived amount differences.

Novel p-methylthio benzaldehyde m129 at 5/1 predicts 10.96/21.79 mL. It adds a second aromatic-sulfide environment and tests the similar endpoints predicted for methylthio aldehyde and ketone structures.

m115 at 5/1 and 100 ul anchors the sulfur-transfer comparisons with a previously observed methoxy-ketone scaffold. Its label also tests transfer from the available 150 ul experiment before structural differences are attributed to O/S substitution.

Novel bis-benzoyl scaffold m178 at 20/1 predicts early onset but prolonged completion, 4.74/32.36 mL, with a broad V1 quantile range. This tests how aromatic carbonyl multiplicity affects the two endpoints.

Novel long-chain dibromothiophene m71 has maximum observed similarity 0.275 and predicts ordinary endpoints of 5.51/8.68 mL in pure EA. It probes a distant sulfur-heterocycle environment despite broad predicted quantile ranges.

Novel compact aliphatic ketone-nitrile m47 has maximum observed similarity about 0.276 and predicts 4.15/8.97 mL at 2/1. It tests transfer from predominantly aromatic carbonyl/nitrile examples into a branched aliphatic environment.

hypotheses.content: The predictor assigns different solvent-response shapes to lutidine, para-aminobenzonitrile and dibenzylamine. These may reflect family-specific adsorption or incorrect structural transfer; matched labels can distinguish the alternatives.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Local response pairs can teach nitrogen-family interactions affecting both onset and completion rather than a single structure-only offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which predicted response changes survive measurement, and do the different nitrogen environments require separate corrections?

hypotheses.content: Near-identical endpoint predictions across controlled sample-amount and loading-volume contrasts may conceal condition-dependent effects of these recorded variables.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Controlled contrasts can determine whether loading features deserve stronger interactions with structure and mobile phase, while allowing that some variation may remain unexplained by the catalog.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do m125 loading-volume changes or m177 sample-amount changes alter either endpoint at 5/1 despite the nearly invariant predictions?

hypotheses.content: Hydroxyl environment and carboxylic-acid character may alter adsorption and solvent response beyond what donor counts capture. Primary alcohols, secondary alcohols, alpha-hydroxy esters and acids may therefore need different representations.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Testing distinct donor environments can improve transfer without assuming a universal retention ordering or ignoring recorded loading differences.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the steep predicted m135 response hold, and how well do alcohol-family relationships transfer to the selected secondary alcohol, hydroxy-ester and acid environments?

hypotheses.content: Some multiacceptor carbonyl candidates have steep predicted condition responses, while others combine early predicted onset with prolonged completion. Measurements may reveal transferable relationships or scaffold-specific extrapolation errors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Carbonyl chemistry occupies much of the catalog. Response pairs and distinct carbonyl environments can inform separate V1 and V2 dependencies across many rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the predicted m13, m39 and m118 response shapes correct, and do m167 and m178 share their endpoint patterns?

hypotheses.content: Replacing aryl methoxy oxygen with methylthio sulfur may change adsorption in ways not captured by acceptor counts, with aldehyde versus ketone environment modulating that transfer.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Two aromatic-sulfide labels accompanied by oxygen-containing references test a specific functional-group transfer gap.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are methylthio aldehyde and ketone endpoints similar at 5/1, and how do they compare with methoxy references after accounting for recorded loading conditions?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback emphasizes scaffold-specific failures: several nitrogen-containing compounds and the nitro-aldehyde example had substantial acquisition-time V2 underprediction, whereas ordinary aromatic controls were often much closer or modestly overpredicted. Those historical errors are not current-model residuals. Current nearby predictions have moved upward, so this batch emphasizes new condition anchors and transfer tests. Feedback also showed that completion can remain inaccurate when onset is close. I treat the loading interpretation as unresolved: prior contrasts varied in direction, and one major comparison changed DCM loading volume rather than sample amount. The matched contrasts test whether those relationships persist across mobile-phase ratios. Higher PE/EA ratios are interpreted as weaker eluent because EA fraction decreases.
batch_rationale: The batch contains seven within-batch solvent-response pairs, controlled loading contrasts, extensions of measured condition curves, and probes of uncovered structural environments. Nitrogen pairs target failure-prone families and transfer to new basic environments. The m13 and oxygen-rich aromatic pairs identify response shapes relevant to the abundant carbonyl rows. Loading contrasts challenge nearly unchanged predictions when sample amount or DCM loading volume changes. Donor-containing rows explore chemically plausible differences among primary alcohols, secondary alcohols, hydroxy esters and acids. Sulfur probes test a focused functional-group transfer question. Distant m47 and m71 supply ordinary-retention probes alongside later predictions. Identical experiment tuples are not repeated within the batch, and comparisons with differing conditions are treated as joint structure-condition evidence rather than isolated causal effects. Quantile widths guide attention without being equated to epistemic uncertainty; V2 minus V1 remains an elution interval. These labels are intended to improve transferable relationships and endpoint calibration across the Row-distribution.
